title: Dengue admissions rise to 1,674 in a day; deaths reach 508
excerpt: One more person died of dengue in the 24 hours to Wednesday morning, and 5,617 patients are still in hospital, DGHS figures show.
content:
Hospitals admitted 1,674 dengue patients in the 24 hours to 8am on Wednesday (18 November), up from 1,537 a day earlier, according to Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) figures reported by bdnews24.com's Bangla edition. One more death, in Dhaka division, took this year's toll to 508.

Dhaka division had the most new admissions (714), followed by Chattogram (311), Barishal (213), Khulna (190), Rajshahi (115), Rangpur (60), Mymensingh (50) and Sylhet (21).

So far this year, 167,318 people have been admitted with dengue and 161,193 have been discharged. 5,617 patients were still in hospital.

State Minister for Health and Family Welfare Dr M A Muhit said on 17 November that all dengue tests are now free at government hospitals and 2,000 doctors have been trained, The Financial Express reported.

Why it matters

Admissions are rising again in mid-November, well past the usual peak, and cases are spread across every division. Health NGOs and community clinics are seeing the load outside Dhaka too.

What to watch

Daily admissions over the next two weeks, as experts have warned of a hard December, and whether free testing reaches upazila level.
